title: Brazil's Presidential Election Heads to a Run-Off
summary:
Brazil held an election for president on Sunday. No one won more than 50 percent of the votes, so there will be a second round of voting on October 25, called a run-off.

Flávio Bolsonaro, a right-wing politician, finished first. He beat Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, the left-wing president who is now in office. Bolsonaro did better than many people expected. His father, Jair Bolsonaro, is a former president. He is serving a 27-year prison sentence for leading a failed coup attempt after losing the last election. He was not allowed to run again, so his son ran instead.

Lula is 80 years old and wants a fourth term. Bolsonaro is 45. After voting, Lula said the choice was between democracy and "barbarism." Bolsonaro said he wanted to "free the Brazilian people."

Voters said the economy, crime and corruption were top concerns. Lula said the United States tried to influence the election. On Sunday, the head of Brazil's top electoral court said no evidence of that was found.

Brazil is the largest country in Latin America.
why_it_matters: Brazil is the biggest country in Latin America, so who its voters choose affects people there and the way countries in the region work together.
